review_candidates.title: Fleet Intelligence Analyst
review_candidates.description: Where passion meets opportunity The best of your adventures is the one you have yet to sail! Your Purpose The global security environment is increasingly volatile, complex, and unpredictable, presenting a dynamic and expanding range of risks to the cruise sector and wider maritime industry. In parallel with the rapid growth of our MSC Cruises and Explora Journeys fleets, our senior leadership requires timely, accurate, and actionable intelligence for agile and effective risk-based decision-making to ensure the highest standards of protection for our guests, people, and assets, around the world. For MSC Cruises and Explora Journeys, this function is delivered by the Fleet Intelligence Team, within the Security Department of MSC Cruises Cruise Management (UK). Operating in a dynamic environment, the Fleet Intelligence Analyst is part of a team that delivers critical intelligence on security, geopolitical, and operational risks, driving informed decision-making and situational awareness across the Fleets and wider Company. Reporting to the Head of Intelligence, and under the day-to-day supervision of the Associate Manager Intelligence & Data Analysis, the Fleet Intelligence Analyst plays a key role in the production and dissemination of intelligence products for a growing, diverse and global stakeholder base. Your Impact Uses all-source intelligence (including alert feeds, traditional and social media, and in-house sources) to monitor security incidents and trends, assessing the likely impact on staff, assets, operations, events, and reputation. Produces timely, concise, and operationally relevant intelligence products to support operational planning and crisis response with rapid intelligence analysis during incidents. Delivers geospatial and visual analysis using standard mapping tools and specialised maritime platforms. Delivers intelligence briefings to senior leadership and operational stakeholders, as directed. Maintains intelligence platforms and continuously reviews intelligence processes, methodologies, and data sources. Your Journey so far Practical experience with open-source intelligence (OSINT) methodologies, sources, and tools Experience with analytical, intelligence, and data visualisation tools and software Strong analytical and critical thinking skills, with a high-level of attention to detail Previous experience in a security or intelligence role within the cruise or wider maritime sector (preferred) Sound understanding of maritime security and operational risk principles (preferred) Experience in statistical analysis and the clear presentation of data insights (preferred) Proficiency in Power BI and other Microsoft Office applications (preferred) Your Essentials The existing right to live and work in the UK. A minimum of five years’ professional experience in a risk intelligence role. Undergraduate degree in a relevant subject, or equivalent vocational qualification. Excellent written and spoken English (Level 5/5). A sound understanding of geo-politics. Our commitment We are committed to building a future that values diverse perspectives, embraces the world beyond borders, and fosters an inclusive environment where every individual feels valued, respected and empowered to be their authentic selves. Our commitment extends to taking meaningful, measurable actions that have a long-term positive impact on our guests, our employees and our planet. Ready to turn your passion into something extraordinary? Join us at MSC Cruises, where new opportunities await. Apply today to be part of a global team that is pushing boundaries and achieving something remarkable. Your journey starts here!

The company focuses on building strong financial foundations to support long-term strategic objectives and operational excellence. Team members collaborate across departments to improve processes, optimize resources, and support data-driven decision-making. Role Description This is a full-time, on-site Finance Manager role based in the Riyadh Region. The Finance Manager will oversee day-to-day financial operations, including budgeting, forecasting, cash flow management, and financial reporting. The role involves preparing and reviewing financial statements, ensuring compliance with relevant regulations and internal policies, and coordinating with external auditors and stakeholders. The Finance Manager will analyze financial performance, identify variances, and propose actions to improve profitability and cost efficiency. This role also includes managing the finance team, refining internal controls, supporting strategic planning, and contributing to key business decisions with clear, data-driven insights. Strong communication skills in English; proficiency in Arabic is beneficial.

The EVP Finance will work closely with the Group CFO, CEO, Board, business-unit CEOs, investment leadership, and senior executives to strengthen financial performance, capital efficiency, profitability, governance, risk management, and long-term enterprise value. Key Responsibilities Lead enterprise-wide financial strategy, planning, budgeting, forecasting, and performance management. Provide executive oversight of financial performance across subsidiaries, business units, and investment platforms. Drive Group-wide FP&A, management reporting, financial modelling, and commercial finance. Monitor revenue, profitability, expenses, margins, cash flow, ROE, ROIC, and return on capital. Oversee financial management of insurance operations, including premiums, claims, reserves, reinsurance, underwriting performance, and profitability. Provide financial leadership for investment and asset management businesses, including portfolio reporting, valuation, investment income, performance analysis, and cost management. Lead strategic capital planning, capital allocation, solvency, liquidity, and balance-sheet optimization. Provide executive oversight of treasury, funding, cash management, and liquidity planning. Establish and strengthen Group-wide financial governance, internal controls, accounting policies, and risk-management frameworks. Ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards, tax requirements, insurance regulations, investment regulations, and statutory reporting requirements. Lead financial evaluation and due diligence for M&A, acquisitions, joint ventures, strategic investments, restructuring, and market expansion. Partner with the Investment, Actuarial, Risk, Compliance, Legal, Treasury, and Operations functions on major strategic and financial decisions. Drive enterprise-wide cost optimization, operational efficiency, and profitability improvement. Lead finance transformation, including ERP modernization, automation, AI/data analytics, dashboards, and digital finance initiatives. Maintain senior relationships with regulators, auditors, investors, lenders, rating agencies, and other financial stakeholders. Provide high-level financial advice to the CEO, Group CFO, Board, and Executive Committee. Build a strong succession pipeline and lead senior finance executives across the organization. Support the development and execution of the Group's long-term growth and value-creation strategy. Strategic KPIs Group revenue and earnings growth EBITDA / operating profit ROE, ROIC, and return on capital Capital adequacy and solvency Investment portfolio performance Insurance underwriting profitability Budget and forecast accuracy Cost-to-income and expense efficiency Liquidity and treasury performance Balance-sheet optimization Cost of capital M&A and strategic investment returns Regulatory and audit performance Finance transformation and automation Shareholder and enterprise value creation Candidate Profile 18–25+ years of progressive finance experience, preferably within insurance, investment management, asset management, banking, reinsurance, pensions, or diversified financial services. Extensive experience in enterprise-level, Group, regional, or multi-entity finance leadership. Previous experience as EVP Finance, Executive Vice President Finance, Group Finance Director, Group CFO, CFO, SVP Finance, Finance Director, Deputy Group CFO, or equivalent. Strong understanding of insurance finance, investment finance, capital management, treasury, financial reporting, and regulatory requirements. Demonstrated experience managing complex organizations with multiple subsidiaries, business lines, and jurisdictions. Strong commercial understanding of investments, financial markets, capital allocation, and enterprise performance. Proven track record in M&A, capital raising, strategic investments, restructuring, or major transformation initiatives. Extensive experience engaging with Boards, CEOs, regulators, investors, auditors, and other senior stakeholders. Proven ability to lead large, geographically dispersed finance organizations. Education & Professional Qualifications Bachelor's or Master's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business, or related discipline. Professional qualification such as CA, ACCA, CPA, CMA, CFA, or equivalent strongly preferred. Additional qualifications in insurance, investments, risk, actuarial science, or financial management are advantageous. review_candidates.title: Chief Financial Officer
review_candidates.description: About The Client Our client is a global payment platform specializing in acquiring, business accounts, and virtual card issuing services for digital businesses. Catering to sectors like e-commerce, iGaming, and finance, they offer secure and compliant payment processing solutions that support both low-risk and high-risk industries. Their services include card processing, mass payouts, open banking, and alternative payment methods, empowering businesses to manage and scale their financial operations efficiently. Role Overview This is an exciting opportunity to lead the financial transformation at a dynamic payment service provider. As the CFO, you will drive the development of the finance function across multiple legal entities. You will play a crucial role in building and automating finance processes, implementing ERP systems, and partnering with senior management to enhance financial visibility and decision-making. Key Responsibilities Lead the transformation and development of the Group’s finance function across multiple legal entities. Build, improve, and automate core finance processes, including month-end closing, consolidation, budgeting, forecasting, and financial reporting. Lead the implementation of ERP and financial management systems and ensure finance processes are structured and scalable. Establish strong internal controls, reporting standards, and processes in line with international best practices. Oversee treasury, safeguarding, regulatory reporting, and external audit processes. Take a hands-on approach during the transformation phase, building the function and processes before moving into a more strategic leadership role. Partner with senior management and other functions to improve financial visibility, controls, and decision-making. Requirements Proven experience in a CFO, Finance Director, or senior finance leadership role, ideally within fintech, payments, banking, or another regulated financial services environment. Strong experience in building and transforming finance functions and processes. Solid IFRS reporting and consolidation experience across multiple legal entities. Experience with ERP and/or FP&A system implementation; NetSuite experience is a plus. Strong understanding of treasury, safeguarding, financial controls, and regulatory requirements. ACA, ACCA, or equivalent professional qualification. Experience with Big4 audits is a plus. Experience in fintech. Key Soft Skills Hands-on, proactive, and highly accountable. Comfortable building processes from scratch and working through operational details rather than simply delegating. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Structured and pragmatic approach to complex challenges. Strong communication and stakeholder management skills. What We Offer Competitive salary aligned with experience. Collaborative and transparent team culture. High-impact role in a scaling fintech company. Recognition of personal milestones and achievements. Social benefits.

review_candidates.description: About Jack Westin Jack Westin is a leading Medical College Admissions Test (MCAT) preparation company which is known for crafting high quality, but free, practice materials. The MCAT tests students on the scientific reasoning skills and scientific knowledge which can be learned during typical undergraduate coursework. Ensures solutions thoroughly explain the reasoning behind the correct answer while clearly addressing why alternative answer choices are incorrect. Reports directly to the Director of Product and Science Content Manager to ensure solutions meet established quality standards, project requirements, and deadlines Employment with Jack Westin may be contingent upon successful completion of background, reference, employment history, education, and credential verification, as applicable and permitted by law. review_candidates.title: Change Manager, Delivery Service Partner
review_candidates.job_function: Project Management, Management, and Product Management
review_candidates.description: Description The Change Manager (CM) serves as a coordinator of transformation across the delivery network. They support projects impacting DSPs, ensuring every transition is smooth, purposeful, and impactful. From the moment a Project Owner (PO) submits a request until after implementation, the CM manages change by using their expertise to distill inputs from stakeholder groups, inform decisions, and recommend solutions. This work is both tactical and operational, requiring them to handle complex problems and escalations with guidance from senior leadership. Their scope spans the delivery ecosystem—from Amazon Logistics (AMZL) and Amazon XL (AMXL) to Same Day (SD), Sub Same Day (SSD), and eventually A-Now and A-Rush operations. With this view, CMs act as guardians of both Delivery Service Partner (DSP) and Delivery Associate (DA) experiences, balancing innovation with operational stability. This role is underpinned by its preventive approach—working closely with stakeholders and operational CMs to identify potential roadblocks before they materialize. When challenges arise, they collaborate with POs to develop mitigation strategies and escalate where necessary. Beyond managing change—they're advocates of Amazon's Day 1 culture, enabling us to innovate at speed and scale whilst ensuring we take the DSPs with us and that pace is sustainable. Key job responsibilities Complexity: The CM navigates and coordinates conflicting priorities to support smooth deployment and communication. They understand the interdependencies of the business problems they help solve (e.g., aligned workflows, customer requirements, process limitations, legal or compliance requirements, program support, etc.) and they contribute data-driven inputs to prioritization. They support the case for project priorities and/or appropriate program adoption to achieve a desired business outcome, resolve a deficiency, or unblock delivery. Scope and Influence: The CM develops working backwards plans for projects to support POs and ensure relevant viewpoints are sought and incorporated into project development prior to deployment. They possess foundational understanding of operational processes and workflow, and they provide guidance to teams and field personnel on their projects. They facilitate projects that feed into manager and director-level goals. Ambiguity: The CM proactively identifies risks and brings them to the attention of the team and stakeholders with proposed plans for mitigation before they become roadblocks. These efforts require them to collaborate with and influence multiple teams, e.g., legal, finance, and pricing, within their organization at the AMET level. Communication: The CM communicates ideas effectively, verbally and in writing, to a range of audiences. They foster constructive dialogue, harmonize discordant views, provide recommendations, and contribute to the resolution of contentious issues. They partner successfully with project and program managers, regional stakeholders, DSPs, and business partner teams. Basic Qualifications 3+ years of program or project management experience Experience implementing repeatable processes and driving automation or standardization Knowledge of Excel at an intermediate level (e.g., pivot tables & charts, multiple criteria lookups, nested logical/IF formulas, data cleansing, array formulas, etc.) Bachelor's degree Preferred Qualifications 2+ years of driving end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership experience 2+ years of driving process improvements experience Experience in stakeholder management, dealing with multiple stakeholders at varied levels of the organization Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. If you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please visit https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations for more information. If the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your Recruiting Partner. Company - Q-Express Documents Transport Job ID: A10507627
